lines.en: Would you like to respond?
: I think you might have sent this to the wrong number.
: Do you not like cats?
: They’re fine. You just don’t really talk to me anymore (for good reason).
: Should I not have sent this to you?
: You actually did it on purpose?
: I thought you might like to see it.
: I like this part a little bit more, admittedly.
: Texting me?
: That was the implication, yes.
: We’ve never really done that before. It feels kind of weird.
: Karin, what’s going on right now? Is everything okay?
: Yeah, I’m fine. Everything’s good.
: I’m just wondering how you’re doing.
: Why? You’re not supposed to care anymore.
: I don’t want to. But I do.
: And I’ve been hearing things lately that make me feel worried.
: About me?
: Yeah.
: Like what? If you don’t mind me asking.
: Like you and Ami getting into a fight. And her leaving.
: You must be lonely. And that makes me feel bad.
: There’s something else too, though.
: Do you remember when we talked near your house? And you told me that sometimes you can’t control yourself?
: I remember saying a lot that day, and I remember you believing almost none of it.
: Because I was mad and I thought you were making up excuses.
: But I heard from Touka that you weren’t lying. And that you do sort of black out sometimes.
: And now you believe it?
: Now, I have a reason to.
: So...you’re not mad anymore?
: I’m still mad.
: You still admitted to feeling a certain way about me that isn’t really okay, Sensei.
: This is probably where we should stop texting. This isn’t the kind of stuff you want on your phone.
: I won’t tell anyone about this and I’ll delete everything after.
: I’d call, but I don’t want to hear your voice.
: Can I just ask you a question, though?
: And I might have already asked it once, but so many things were happening back then that I can barely remember anything.
: Do you regret it?
: Even if it was something you couldn’t control? Do you feel bad that it happened?
: Of course. I never wanted to hurt you. You’re like the only person I know who’s never done anything wrong.
: I had no idea how scary you could be.
: Well, now you do. And now you probably won’t send me any more pictures of cats you find.
: Are you still going to the beach with your class? Even though Ami left and you’re not teaching anymore?
: I’m not sure yet. Why?
: I’m going.
: Trying to figure out where and when to avoid running into me?
: I won’t do that. I just don’t want to be blindsided again.
: I’m mad, yeah. But I’m mostly just upset that things are the way they are now.
: I miss when we were normal.
: You still are. I’m the one who fucked up, accidental or not.
: I don’t feel like I am. It’s harder to be happy now.
: And my heart keeps telling me to forgive you, but thinking about listening to it makes me sick to my stomach.
: I don’t want to feel this way anymore. But I don’t know what to do about it.
: I’m not really sure what to say to you here, Karin.
: If you see me again
: Can you talk to me?
: Really?
: I won’t do it on my own.
: I just think that maybe it will make me feel kind of normal again.
: I don’t know.
: I have to go, though. I’m making dinner tonight.
: Goodnight, Sensei.
: I’m sorry you’re unhappy right now.
: Goodnight, Karin...
: Thanks.
